liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Shakedown Street** (2 reviews, 1 other source): Phil's loud bass bombs during Shakedown Street were likened to a Southern California earthquake; Reviewer calls this their favorite Shakedown Street, and says the show is on a Dead video release [6][11][13]
- **Looks Like Rain** (1 review): Reviewer singles out Bob Weir's performance on Looks Like Rain as excellent [13]
- **The Other One** (1 review): Reviewer found the second-set Other One very strong, high-energy and on fire [19]
- **Not Fade Away** (1 review): Reviewer found the second-set Not Fade Away very strong and high-energy [19]
- **Chimes Of Freedom** (1 review): Reviewer praises rarer Dylan material such as Chimes of Freedom [14]
- **All Along The Watchtower** (1 review): Reviewer calls Watchtower terrific, noting it was chosen for the album release [14]

## Setlist highlights

- **Mr Tambourine Man**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]
- **Dead Man, Dead Man**: rare: 3 archived performances [23]
- **Simple Twist Of Fate**: rare: 4 archived performances [23]
- **Watching The River Flow**: rare: 3 archived performances [23]
- **Chimes Of Freedom**: rare: 6 archived performances [23]
- **Ballad Of A Thin Man**: rare: 10 archived performances [23]
- **Rainy Day Women #12 And #35**: rare: 4 archived performances [23]
- **Gotta Serve Somebody**: rare: 3 archived performances [23]

## The recordings

- **gd1987-07-26.141759.sbd.miller.flac2496** (recommended): soundboard; 32 songs; 229 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [1]
- **gd1987-07-26.148616.mtx.tobin.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 32 songs; 225 min [3]
- **gd1987-07-26.aud.seaweed.124098.flac1644**: audience recording; 32 songs; 221 min; rated 1.33/5 by 3 [4]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls this audience recording poor and suggests finding a better source [21]
- **gd1987-07-26.148618.5-1.tobin.flac1648**: source not stated; 32 songs; 225 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [5]
- **gd1987-07-26.nak700.yamaguchi-poris.russjcan.98214.flac16**: source not stated; 31 songs; 217 min; rated 3.54/5 by 13 [6]. Said about its sound: The start of Mr. Tambourine Man is cut on this recording [6]
- **gd1987-07-26.sbd-set3.unknown.97495.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 15 songs; 90 min; rated 3.8/5 by 5 [9]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the bass muddy and the crowd screaming loudly from all directions on this matrix [16]

## Around the show

- Attendee saw it as one of three West Coast shows; recalls Weir wearing a Madonna t-shirt; stadium acoustics poor [14]
- Attendee recalls fighting in the front row, Weir distracted, hot weather, and heavy LSD use among the crowd [17]
- Early disorder with clashes between fans and security settled down, and the show turned out well [17]
- Attendee from a sober living house recalls pot and crack smoking nearby, and an improvised NA meeting near orange balloons in the outfield [22]
- Notes describe a third set with Bob Dylan joining the band [1]
- Reviewer says the rest of the show is less noteworthy than the second set [19]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1987-07-26.141759.sbd.miller.flac2496**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK MA-R90) [1]
- **gd1987-07-26.148616.mtx.tobin.flac16**: transferred by SBD + AUD Matrix 3 Source Mix (44/16) by Kevin Tobin; source: SBD + AUD Matrix 3 Source Mix (44/16) [3]. Also: Mix featuring Dylan's guitar in set 3, made by an archive.org user, converted to FLAC December 2019 [3]
- **gd1987-07-26.aud.seaweed.124098.flac1644**: transferred by seaweed; source: Source: 1x Sennheiser MD-421 (mono) > unknown deck > MAC, recorded "off second stack behind Healy". 1st Gen cassettes kindly provided by Seaweed1010. [4]
- **gd1987-07-26.148618.5-1.tobin.flac1648**: transferred by 5.1 LPCM Surround Sound Mix (48k) by Kevin Tobin; source: 5.1 LPCM Surround Sound Mix (48k) [5]. Also: 5.1 surround mix of the Dylan set 3 songs, made in Adobe Audition by an archive.org user [5]
- **gd1987-07-26.nak700.yamaguchi-poris.russjcan.98214.flac16**: taped by Tazuo Yamaguchi and Jamie Poris; transferred by Russ Cansler; source: Modified Nak 700's omni with Sony D5 FOB Spread 6 feet apart [6]. Also: Encore source is Nak 300 tapes, second generation; placed at the end of disk 1 [6]
- **gd1987-07-26.sbd-set3.unknown.97495.shnf**: source: Soundboard (audience starting with Ballad of a Thin Man) [9]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Anaheim Stadium - July 26, 1987](https://www.dead.net/show/july-26-1987) [25]
- Poster by Robbi Cohn: [1987-07-26 Anaheim Stadium, Anaheim, CA, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1987-07-26-anaheim-stadium-anaheim-ca-usa/) [26]
- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead BGP Staff Laminate, Back. Bob Dylan/Grateful Dead, Anaheim Stadium](https://www.dead.net/archives/1987/clippings/bgp-staff-laminate-back-bob-dylan-grateful-dead-anaheim-stadium) [27]
- Poster by Robbi Cohn: [1987-07-26 Anaheim Stadium, Anaheim, CA, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1987-07-26-anaheim-stadium-anaheim-ca-usa/) [28]
- Fan art by smarturl.it: [Bob Dylan, Grateful Dead - Knockin' on Heaven's Door - Live at Anaheim Stadium, Anaheim, CA - July 1987](https://smarturl.it/7knockhea_dead) [29]
- Poster by Jam Buzz: [Listen to the Grateful Dead and Bob Dylan’s Finale in Anaheim on This Day – 7/26/1987 Soundboard](https://jam.buzz/grateful-dead-7-26-1987-soundboard/) [30]
